draft.title: Graphs and conclusions
card: Column graph
Use it when the data is in separate categories, such as the colour of flowers or the type of pet. Each category gets its own column.
Line graph
Use it when the data is measured values that change, such as temperature over time. The independent variable goes on the x-axis and the dependent variable on the y-axis.
Trend
A trend is the pattern in the data. For example, the line may rise, fall or stay flat as the independent variable changes.
Conclusion
A conclusion uses the trend to answer the aim. It states what the data shows, and it only claims what the results support.

2.alt: A line graph of water temperature in degrees Celsius against time in minutes. The line rises steadily from 20 degrees at 0 minutes to 60 degrees at 8 minutes.

draft.remember: Pick the graph to suit the data. Then use the trend to answer the aim.

a.q: Which data would be best shown on a line graph?
opts: The height of a plant measured each day for 10 days
The number of students who chose each school sport
The favourite fruit of each student in a class
The number of cars of each colour in a car park
a.why: Plant height is a measured value that changes over time, so a line graph shows the trend. The other options sort things into separate categories, which suit column graphs.
a.clue: Look for a measurement that changes as something else changes.

b.q: Ravi's aim was to find out if more sunlight makes bean seedlings grow taller. His graph shows seedling height rising as hours of sunlight per day increase. Which conclusion fits his data?
opts: Seedlings grew taller as the hours of sunlight increased
Sunlight is the only thing that makes any plant grow
Seedlings grew taller as the hours of sunlight decreased
Seedlings of all kinds grow best in very long daylight
b.why: The trend is that height rises as sunlight hours rise, and this answers the aim. The option about all plants goes beyond bean seedlings, so the data does not support it. Reversing the trend contradicts the graph.
b.clue: A conclusion must match the trend and only claim what was tested.

a.best: The height of a plant measured each day for 10 days

b.best: Seedlings grew taller as the hours of sunlight increased

problems.detail: Why (b) refers to 'the option about all plants' as if there were only one. Two distractors overreach: 'Sunlight is the only thing that makes any plant grow' and 'Seedlings of all kinds grow best in very long daylight'. The explanation should say why both are wrong.

check.summary: The card, graph and both questions are accurate, and the intended answers are correct. The only issue is minor: why (b) speaks of a single 'all plants' option when two distractors overgeneralise.
